utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The cross-examination by Mr. Hannis will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you gave at the outset continues to apply to your evidence until it's completed. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to start off this morning showing you an exhibit, it's number P1421, 1421, it will be up on your screen in a moment, General, it's a 7 August 1998 order on further engagement of the army forces in Kosovo, and it's from the 3rd Army commander, General Samardzic. I see on your screen we have the second page, and we see that it did go apparently to the 125th Brigade by telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And now if we could go to the first page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, do you recall receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 it makes reference to: "According to the approved decision, army units are to be engaged as support to the MUP ..." Do you know what that's a reference to? Do you know what "approved decision" General Samardzic is talking about there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the decision that he approved for the benefit of the corps commander. I know that the army commander or his Chief of Staff spent some time in Pristina at the Kosovo's heroes barracks sometime during 1998. This used to be the forward command post of the 3rd Army, and he met the corps commander on a daily basis to hand out assignments to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In item number 3 it talks about the ZTJ, the Joint Tactical Units. Can you explain to us what they are and how that differs from the battle groups or the combat groups?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means combined tactical unit, and it has the rank of an independent battalion in a brigade. And a combat group is a temporary unit that is set up within these combined tactical groups in order to lend support or to provide -- to secure the state border down the depth. That's the first thing. And secondly, there was that approved decision by the Supreme Defence Council and there were orders by the 3rd Army and support was lent by these units to the MUP based on those decisions in certain actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I need a little further help from you. We see in a number of the Joint Command orders, Pristina Corps command orders, and your own 125th Brigade orders references to BG-1, I think up to as high at one point in time as BG-6 within the 125th. Is that right? Did you at one time have as many as six combat groups?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just before the war broke out I had six combat groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, were your combat groups part of this -- of a joint tactical unit; and if so, what was the rest of the composition of a joint tactical unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combined arms tactical units had their own type of establishment and organization. Combat groups are set up by using units, regular units, including both officers and NCOs and also from this combined set-up from these tactical units. They usually have the rank of a reinforced company. They are smaller units than a battalion or a division perhaps, and the most -- the best trained elements of a battalion or a division are used to organize these combined arms tactical units. I'm not sure if this is a sufficient explanation for you, sir, if you want me to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm still a little confused. Let me try and break it down this way. Within the 125th you had, as we said, up to six combat groups. What was the -- generally speaking, what was the composition of a combat group within your 125th? Approximately how many men and how many and what kinds of vehicles and weaponry did they consist of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow, let's consider the example of Combat Group 1, which was about 220 strong. It had a motorised company comprising about 160 men. This motorised company contained three firing platoons and there was a support platoon as well comprising recoilless guns for artillery weapons and a platoon of 82-millimetre mortars with four individual weapons. It also has a platoon of 120-millimetre guns, two of those, and there was also -- there was a 120-millimetre howitzer battery as well as a logistical platoon, a rear platoon, if you like. So that would be its composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That helps. Now, the joint tactical units referred to in this order, what were they composed of? Were they composed of one or more battle groups? Would they contain only battle groups from one brigade or would they cross brigades? And did they contain anything other than VJ components?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I must say I'm understanding this the other way around, Mr. Hannis, that the tactical units are the more permanent ones and the combat groups are the more temporary ones, so it's a -- part of the tactical unit might be used to form a combat group but not the other way around. However, if that's wrong, no doubt the witness will tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm hoping he will explain because in item number 3 here it seems to read the other way to me, but I'm sure the General can help us understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll certainly do my best. A combined arms tactical unit is a part of the permanent organizational set-up. I can't remember specifically now, but it has both a wartime and a peacetime establishment which cannot be changed without a decision by the General Staff. Specifically the 125th Motorised Brigade, under its peacetime establishment, had a command. As for units, it had two motorised battalions. I'm just stating this one example of Kosovska Mitrovica where there was one of them and then another one was in Pec, it had an armoured battalion in Pec. It had a howitzer division in Kosovska Mitrovica, it had an anti-armour division in Kosovska Mitrovica, and so on and so forth. Well, okay. Now, if you wish to set up a combat group what you have is this, combat groups are elements or units that are set up pursuant to a decision on special measures of ongoing combat-readiness. Now I'm introducing another term, special measures of combat-readiness. The meaning behind this is to take a certain number of men from the 1st Battalion that is stationed in Kosovska Mitrovica and use these as a basis for setting up Combat Group 1. Naturally what is attached here is elements from the howitzer battalion, from the rear battalion, and then all of that, and what this is used for, these best-trained men who had completed top-level training, they are used for interventions along axes that are at particular risk, especially along the state border. And there is nothing else here apart from this military set-up that is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I guess I'm still not clear, and I would ask you in your next answer if you could speak a little more slowly I think for the interpreters you went pretty fast on that last one.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Within the Pristina Corps, how many joint tactical units were there in 1998 during peacetime?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't give you specific figure, but I can list them for you, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 125th Brigade; the 549th Motorised Brigade; the 243rd Mechanised Brigade; the 15th Armoured Brigade; the 52nd Mixed Artillery Brigade; the 52nd Artillery Rocket Brigade, anti-aircraft defence. I'm not sure if I'm forgetting something. That should be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, that sounds then as though a brigade is considered a joint tactical unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, that's right, but that's what I said at the outset, didn't I? Something that has the rank of a regiment or possibly a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let me go then to page 2 of this document in both the B/C/S and the English. In item number 7 General Samardzic says: "I forbid units to be used contrary to this order. "If orders are received to use units contrary to this order, unit commanders who receive such orders shall immediately inform the second superior officer and act according to his orders." First let me ask you, General, in this context: Who would be your second superior officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context my second superior officer, superior to me, would be the undersigned commander, Colonel-General Dusan Samardzic, 3rd Army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And at this time your first superior officer was General Pavkovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is this -- is this a standard provision in orders like this? It seems unusual to me.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't frequent, that much is certain; but it's perfectly in keeping with the rules. You can't challenge your second superior or third superior, in this case the Chief of the General Staff. They are authorised to exercise command over individual units and men. The Chief of Staff [as interpreted] called me personally using our communications equipment in order to hand out specific assignments to me directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, part of the reason I --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, just one correction in transcript. When the witness mentioned -- I'm sorry. Your Honour, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Seventh page, line 5 and 6 when the witness mentioned "Chief of Staff" he mentioned it of General Staff not just the Chief of Staff, because we have in armies, in corps also Chief of Staff, just to distinguish, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, the reason I ask, item number 8 indicates that: "This order is to be delivered to the Pristina Corps commander," General Pavkovic, "personally and then to the commanders of the directly subordinated units of the Pristina Corps ..." Prior to this date of 7 August 1998, are you aware, had General Samardzic had any kind of problems with General Pavkovic using the subordinate units contrary to the manner that General Samardzic wanted them to be used? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can't be a simple yes or no I'm afraid. I don't know that he had any problems. As far as I know, General Pavkovic did not use his units in a way that was contrary to the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in 1998 or 1999, before the war, were you aware of any concerns at the level of the General Staff of the army about how units were being used in Kosovo? Did you ever hear about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't down to me as a brigade commander to deal with matters such as these, so I never heard anything about that. There is no hearsay in the army, you see. You have orders, you have reports, you have an official exchange of notes and letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zivanovic, that can't possibly be right in view of the terms of this paragraph that we're looking at: "I forbid units to be used contrary to this order. "If orders are received to use units contrary to this order, unit commanders who receive such orders shall immediately inform the second superior officer and act according to his orders." Why on earth would you put that in a document unless somebody had been breaking the rules or you anticipated that the rules would be broken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, this is a perfectly usual document by the 3rd Army commander. He's perfectly authorised to do this. Secondly, if he forbids the use of a unit without his approval, I don't need to know whether General Pavkovic in fact requested authorisation from General Samardzic to use Combat Group 1 from the 125th Brigade. You see, this document was delivered to the corps commander personally, and it was -- it said: "To the attention of the following," which included us. If we had any need to use this combat group, I would have called up the commander of the Pristina Corps; and I would have asked his permission. I suppose the corps commander would have requested the permission of the army commander and then the same thing happens the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me try to understand this completely. Have you on other occasions seen a provision identical to or very similar to paragraph 7 of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you ask me, this is perfectly fine, paragraph 7, it's fine. I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please answer my particular question. It may be that he was entitled to put that in. He's probably entitled to put in it whatever he wants in view of his position. What I want to know is whether you've seen a document of this nature with that sort of provision in it before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go back to page 1 in both the B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I've got another question for you, General. You'll see in the introductory paragraph it says: "On the basis of analysis of the army units' engagement in Kosovo so far," and then it goes on to talk about "pressure from the international community and to regulate more specifically the engagement of the armed forces in accordance with the stands of the state and military leadership, I hereby order:" And number 1 says: "From now on, reinforced army units engaged in Kosovo ... are to be used to secure the state border and military facilities of special importance ..." Reading that all together with number 7 and number 8 that we just talked about, it sounds like something different has been going on prior to the 7th of August, 1998, and that's why General Samardzic feels a need to issue this order at this time. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a legitimate assumption, but I'm not sure where it was exactly that we exceeded our authority or did anything wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let me go now to another exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do that. Mr. Zivanovic, when you said earlier that the Chief of the General Staff called you personally using your communications equipment to hand out specific assignments, was that in relation to this document or was it in relation to some other matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just out of curiosity, General, what was that other matter and when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened on several occasions. The other matter would have been an order or a request to preserve manpower, to take special care of preserving manpower and equipment, to take control of particularly dominant facilities such as Volujak above Klina in order to prevent any manoeuvring by the terrorist forces, and there may have been other details involved that I can't quite remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. On those occasions when you were contacted directly by the General Staff, would you report that to General Pavkovic, that you had been contacted from that level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever a superior officer who is above Pavkovic issues an order to me, I inform my own direct superior, General Pavkovic in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I want to show you P1422. This is also dated the 7th of August, 1998, and this is from General Pavkovic and it goes to the subordinate units on the last page. I will tell you, you can see it goes to the 125th. Do you recall receiving this order? It lists a number of things.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received this, but maybe you could show me the last page, you will see whether it was sent to me as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we show page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we go back to page 1, the introductory paragraph says in part, General, that: "The latest operations carried out by units of the corps in coordinated action with units of the Serbian MUP in curbing terrorism," it says: "An analysis of the achievement of the tasks showed that some units overused combat equipment," and it talked about "a large number of houses were destroyed and torched," and mentions the complaints of the international community. So as a consequence, General Pavkovic is issuing this order, in item number 2, forbidding torching of houses; and in item 3 he says: "I again warn unit commanders and prohibit the taking of personal property from abandoned houses, as was the case in the 125th, 549th," et cetera. Prior to August 7th, General, had there been some problems in your subordinate units with looting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't about large-scale looting. There were problems in Brovina and Molic. The road was blocked on the outskirts of Junik, and we reviewed our soldiers and officers. We ascertained that some of them had in their possession certain items that had been picked up in those houses along the way, so we returned those items, and I initiated disciplinary proceedings against those persons. And after that, an order came on what exactly to do next.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And isn't it correct that during the rest of 1998 and in 1999, before and during the war, that there were many instances of looting by VJ personnel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday how many cases I had prosecuted, about 30 cases of theft. There may have been cases that had slipped our attention, but whenever we knew that something had occurred, we would always press charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I'm not trying to single out your unit. This was a problem throughout the army, right? Your unit wasn't exceptional in terms of being bad for looting. This was something that happened in all units, correct? Or do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but all I'm talking about is my own unit, Mr. Hannis. I'm in no position to talk about, for example, Mr. Jelic's unit and whether there were cases of theft there. I suppose he's in possession of that sort of information, and I suppose that he eventually pressed charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go now to another document, Exhibit P1426. General, I can actually hand you a hard copy of this one, it's a telegram. Maybe it's easier to read the hard copy. This is dated the 8th of August, 1998, and it appears to be a telegram from you to the Pristina Corps command and the forward command post in response to an order from the Pristina Corps command about engagement of MUP units in late July 1998 and early August. Do you recall sending this report to the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from reading this it appears that some of your combat groups worked with various PJP detachments, the 3rd, the 4th, the 7th, and something called the Brazil Group, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My combat group supported these detachments and the Brazil Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what the Brazil Group was or who comprised the Brazil Group. I know at the very end of the telegram there's a description, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Brazil Group was a special anti-terrorist unit. That was the information I had at the time. It was one of the best-trained units within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, now you said "special anti-terrorist unit," is that the SAJ, S-A-J, as we refer to it here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I saw them and that's how they introduced themselves to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In this document, though, they're referred to as JSO, Special Operations Unit.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see it says that here, JSO. The operations officer compiled the report. I just gave him the guide-lines, the bullet points. This is a telegram sent to the communications means using Morse code.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I know you talked briefly about this in your testimony in Haradinaj. I think the reference is transcript pages 9375 through 9378, and at that time you explained that you were sure that the Brazil Group was a SAJ unit and not JSO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's what I said and I abide by that. That was an anti-terrorist unit, a special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, it's my understanding the JSO is from the state security side of the Ministry of Interior, whereas the SAJ is a part of the public security side. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on I made that distinction. At first I myself wasn't aware of all the structures that existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I understand that the JSO sometimes is referred to by some people as it -- as the Red Berets. Were you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw them wearing red berets, except on a film when in 2001 they protested in Belgrade. In the course of 1998 and 1999, they wore normal uniforms with caps the same colour as the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you ever hear them referred to as Frenki's, stemming from the fact that Frenki Simatovic was a commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was something I wondered about when I was given the task of contacting them personally when they were in the area or through my liaison officers, when they were in the Decani area. I didn't know who Frenki was nor have I ever seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who gave you the task of contacting them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been the corps commander. They were in my peacetime area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And approximately when was that, that you were tasked to contact them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in April 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you have contact with any JSO personnel in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many times and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three times, three times, twice in the area between Decani and the border and once in Drenica on the Likovac axis, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what were the circumstances? Were you supporting them in any actions they were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my combat group provided support for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see any JSO in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999 I did not have any contact with them, any personal contact that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you hear about them being present in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I think they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see or hear of any paramilitary groups in Kosovo, first of all, during the pre-war period between the summer of 1998 and March 23rd of 1999, such as Arkan's or Seselj's, Skorpions, Phantoms? Any of those did you come across?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about in 1999 after the war started, after the NATO bombing started, between March and June 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear of them nor did I see anything like that in my area of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. On page 1 of that telegram - I'm not sure if it's on page 1 of the B/C/S - where it mentions that the Brazil Group was 106 men. It says: "They carried out deep wedging and burning operations on all axes ..." Do you find that? I think it's near the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you explain for us what "wedging and burning" is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Haradinaj case I explained what it means, wedging and burning, and I drew a diagram. I will attempt to reproduce my explanation now. What it means is that in the area occupied by Siptar terrorist forces or a building [as interpreted] occupied by them, the special anti-terrorist unit manages to drive a wedge in with the support of people at the side and -- or over heads, and thus manages to take the building or area. The wedge is about 10 or 15 metres deep, and the support -- between 10 and 50 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- metres deep, and the support provided means that there is at least one bullet covering every square inch. That's what burning through means. It's a term invented by the commander of the combat group, my commander of the combat group.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, just one correction in transcript, page 16, line 20, the witness said "prostorija," which doesn't mean building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Area, it means area. It is the military term, area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Ground area or land area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, the English records you as saying: "What it means is that in the area occupied by the Siptar terrorist forces or a building occupied by them, the special anti-terrorist unit manages to drive a wedge ..." Did you refer to a building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether I said "building." I did say "area," meaning an area of land. The wedging-in was not something that was desirable in a built-up area because then there would be huge losses from surrounding buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On -- could you go to page two of that document, General. It mentions that the Brazil Group --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's one other expression in the transcript I find odd. You're recorded as saying that: "The support provided means that there is at least one bullet covering every square inch ..." Now, I'm surprised at a Serb talking about square inches. Could you tell me again what you said once the wedge was driven in, the support provided means there is at least one bullet covering what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said "decimetre," square decimetre, a length of 10 to 50 metres every decimetre, that's 500. Every decimetre has to be covered by at least one bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean -- what do you mean by one bullet? Do you mean one person? If everybody fires together, the area covered by one of your -- or one of their men would be that area? It's an expression I don't really understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to explain, Your Honour. It means that one fighter, one soldier of mine or a member of the MUP can fire from an automatic rifle 20 bullets. With those 20 bullets, he can cover half a metre in width. So to cover 50 metres, you would need a hundred men to be firing simultaneously; but you can't use just one bullet, you have to keep holding the line until the men are through. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is clear now. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That sounds like a very lethal process for anyone in the area that's being wedged and burned, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's supposed to be lethal. It's also lethal for those who are crawling towards that area, who are defending themselves from Siptars, from the terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Page 2 makes reference to the Brazil Group using multiple rocket-launchers. Can you describe for us what those are. Are we talking about something that's mounted on a vehicle? This is not some kind of hand-held weapon, right, this is a big weapon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw that they had an improvised thing. You would put it on a trailer. It was hauled on a trailer. They had rocket-launchers with four to -- or eight barrels, I can't remember which exactly now. I think it was four barrels, and it was not within the army standards, it didn't meet army standards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And in item 1.4 it says in the last sentence: "The only prohibited equipment used were the 122-millimetre howitzers." Why was that prohibited equipment? That was something that had been ordered not to be used without special permission from the commander of the 3rd Army, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's why it was banned. After this analysis, I held Major Bacevic responsible for using that, the commander. I was responsible to General Pavkovic, and I had to make a statement; and I suffered certain consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What is the range on the 122-millimetre howitzer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The howitzers we had in the brigade had a 17-kilometre range with a full charge, but usually it was less. In this case they were used at a range of 4 kilometres to provide support to the special anti-terrorist units in the area so they could pierce through. They were -- one platoon was used in the open -- in the open, out in the open.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Salvo, not platoon. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Item -- the last item, number 4, you mentioned that one of the biggest problems in coordination between MUP units and our -- was between MUP units and your combat vehicles "because MUP members have not been trained to work with" them "and are afraid of potential consequences." Could you explain that for us, what kind of vehicles are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A combat vehicle is either a 90-millimetre self-propelled weapon or a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could I show you -- let me show you three different photographs or exhibits with photographs and ask you if you can help us with that. Exhibit 1325 -- P1325, first of all. I take it, General, you were familiar with all the various combat vehicles, transport vehicles used by the JNA in 1998 and 1999, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless I've forgotten, but we'll see that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. At this photograph we have four different vehicles numbered 1 to 4. Can you tell us what each one of them is and who used them, whether it was the VJ or the MUP or both.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first picture is taken only from the side. It would be easier to recognise if it was taken from the back also. Let's leave it aside for the moment. Number 2 is a command vehicle used only by the army. It's a command transporter. It's used by the army for the battalion commander or division commander and in reconnaissance units. This sort of vehicle has the brigade commander and communications equipment in it. 3 is an M-60 armoured personnel carrier and the special police units in Kosovo and Metohija also had that, the permanent MUP units in Kosovo and Metohija, the PJP that is. And I don't know whether in the 243rd Mechanised Brigade they had those or not, but I don't think they did. Picture number 4, that's a so-called Praga, and both the special police -- the PJP units and the army had that. And as for number 1, I think it's an infantry combat vehicle, M-80, and only the army had those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Number 2, is there a designator for that vehicle? Is there an abbreviation for that or an acronym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, KOT, command armoured personnel carrier, I think that's what it is, or a reconnaissance car, IA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And number 4, the Praga, what kind of weapon is that that's mounted on it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a two-barrel cannon 30-millimetre cannon, and it's intended to fire at targets in the air; but it can also be used to target targets on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record before we go to the next page, picture 3 does appear to have a sign on the front indicating "Derventa," which is not in the Republic of Serbia or Kosovo for that matter, it's relating to one of the other wars on the premises of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, General, on this page could we do the same process, numbers 5 through 8, if you could explain what it is and tell us what is was called, what acronym was used with regard to each of those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Picture number 5, it's an M-84 tank. Picture number 6 is a T-55 tank. Picture 7 is a Pinzgauer; it's used to transport personnel. And I think number 8 is also a Pinzgauer with the canvass, tarpaulin, down. And it could also be a TAM T-7 with the canvass taken down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I take it that only the army had the tanks that are shown in pictures 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As for the --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 7 and 8, both the army and the MUP had those, the PJP that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think there's one more page of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at the next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you help us with these, General?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about number 9, I don't know the precise name. Number 10, I think it's either a police armoured combat vehicle. Number 11, I'm not sure, I didn't see those around. And number 12, I think that's a reconnaissance car or an amphibian, perhaps, vehicle because I can see that it has those holes at the side, propellers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, General, thank you. Next I'd like to show you Exhibit P1597, only two more photos, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can rotate that 90, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of vehicle that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a Praga. I've already mentioned the Praga; I don't remember what number it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I think you told us that both the MUP and the VJ had Pragas in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some units within the PJP, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And next P1598, last one. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is M-84 tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you able to tell from this photograph what kind of uniforms those men are wearing? Are those VJ uniforms or police uniforms or can you tell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the colours are right, this does not look to me like an army uniform, it's darker.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who had uniforms like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember such light blue camouflage uniforms. I know the MUP had blue uniforms, but this is something in between ours and theirs. When I say "ours," I mean army, between army and police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have a question -- just a general question. I see they're wearing what appear to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, an objection in principle. Are we allowed to know the source of this photograph, where and when it was taken? Because we have had certain experience so far with photographs on which we saw five-pointed stars, that is, the JNA before 1991; we had vehicles marked "Derventa" or with licence plates "Derventa," and Derventa is not at all on the territory of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, can you help Mr. Cepic, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have that information to hand, but I don't think it's pertinent for the purposes that I'm asking these questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's pertinent for someone who might want to challenge what you're doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he can look at a uniform from any era and say it was like uniforms in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the other hand, if you have information about the source of this photograph, then it does enable Defence to carry out other investigations that they might wish to do. So I think you ought to do what you can to assist Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My case manager is working on that right now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if I may I'd like to ask a general question then about the ribbons. You see these men have white and red ribbons on their shoulders. I understand that sometimes that was done during combat to avoid the problem of friendly fire. First of all, is that correct in 1998 and 1999 in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered yesterday that we did not use ribbons in my brigade. We had passwords and code-names for that purpose, but now after the intervention of Mr. Cepic and your question and on the basis of this uniform that I cannot identify, I am beginning to think that this is a picture made at a tactical drill in peacetime that the army performed and they found some suits used as designators. Such were used in peacetime at drills with lethal charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I understand you had told us before that your unit did not use such identifiers during combat actions. Are you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, and I'm not aware that others did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you're not aware that other VJ units and/or MUP units in other areas may have used ribbons identifiers like that during combat actions in 1998 and/or 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know. I don't know of any document from the corps command ordering these identifiers to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you never heard of that happening among either the police or the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not in the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple more questions about the Brazil Group. During 1998 and 1999, did you, General, use radio call-signs or code-names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, code-names.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what code-name was used in connection with the 125th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First of all, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you Exhibit P1052. Do you recall what the radio call-sign was for the Pristina Corps, the Pristina Corps command or the forward command post in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure, maybe Kosmos.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm afraid our English page and our B/C/S page don't match up. The matching page for that B/C/S page I believe is the third page in the English. Yes. General, you see this? This is described as a communications plan and it has listed Battle Group 1 of the 125th with the code-name of Ibar 40. Is that consistent with your memory of the code-names -- the code-name used by Battle Group 1 in late 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And there are references to three MUP units and the Joint Command. Do you recall seeing or hearing that code-name "Pastrik" used in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the code-name Pastrik, but this correspondence plan of the army is not for the period. It could be a correspondence plan, a work-plan, for exercises, jamming, radiogoniometry, and other exercises. And when you see the sentence "Pastrik," nobody will answer. It's a general term for the administration station. You can call Pastrik all day and nobody will respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: When did your unit work with the Brazil Group? Was it only in July and August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. July I'm not sure about, August I don't remember. I worked with them. I think it was somewhere end July/beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of the B/C/S. And I think the corresponding English page is page 1. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, you see this one, and next to the --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next to the last on the list is SAJ and then (F) with a code-name Brazil. Would this not be referring to the Brazil Group that you worked with in July and August 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I am not disputing what is written, but you see that there's a SAJ, Special Anti-Terrorist Unit. But what this F in quotation marks means, does it mean that these are Frenki's men, I don't know that. What matters to me is SAJ, Special Anti-terrorist Unit. I don't remember this work-plan for the station, and I'm telling you that there should be an indication for the period from/to, and there should be some more information at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, we don't appear to have that information on this page, but I see that we have Battle Group 1 for the 125th with a call-sign Ibar 80. That's the code-name that battle group used in July and August of 1998, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not the first, it's the third combat group. Yes, among other things, they used such a name but it also used other code-names. We changed them almost every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Changed them from Ibar or changed the number?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We changed it to Ibar. I was administrative Belgrade 13. He was depending on the commander, if it was an armoured battalion commander I called him Medved, bear, 80, because he was on the skinny side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Could we go to the third page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not understanding this. Is this important, Mr. Hannis? Because if it is, I'm not understanding these numbers. If they are important, we need to be clearer. Does Ibar last for a certain number of months or a period of time, is it only the figures that changed. Your question wasn't answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I asked him what code-name he used in 1998, he said Ibar; in 1999 he used another one Barut. So I take it from that Ibar is the code-name for 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have these answers, but we've just heard that the code-name was changed almost every day and you asked: Changed them from Ibar or changed the number. And the answer was: "We changed it to Ibar. It was administrative Belgrade 13." If you're happy with that, that's fine, you move on; but I'm now confused after being clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, for how long a period was the code-name Ibar used and associated with elements of the 125th Motorised Brigade in 1998? Are you telling us it was only used for a day or two, or wasn't it in fact used throughout 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go into such details. There were technical people who dealt with that. I believe Ibar was used for over half a year, but Ibar means administrative station, the part of the hub that is below the command in the basement where the servers are. So it's a stationary communication centre, and that's the one that has the name Ibar. And every server in the command has its own identification with number. You cannot call out "Ibar," nobody will respond. It has to be Ibar 58, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And one other answer you gave with regard to the SAJ, you suggested the possibility that F might stand for Frenki's, but I understood from what you told us before SAJ was part of the public security side of the Ministry of Interior and Frenki Simatovic was on the state security side with the JSO. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made that distinction later for myself. SAJ is MUP and what did we say, JSO is the State Security Service, DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And MUP as I understand it includes both the state security side, the SDB, and the public security side, the SJB. Isn't that right? Ministry of the Interior includes both of them, no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that such distinction, such a division existed in 1998/1999. I believe the state security was elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you the last page of these communication plans --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before moving on. In view of your lack of knowledge of the distinction within the Ministry of the Interior, were there times when you may have been confusing a special anti-terrorist unit with a JSO unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When we get to know each other before an action in which we support that unit, they would introduce themselves. And it is clearly said here, I am such and such a person and I am a special anti-terrorist unit or a part thereof. Maybe on my side I had some doubts, but when they introduced themselves that was cleared up. I don't believe they would hold themselves out to be something they were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we have no explanation for the F in that case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said. I believe that this might be -- imply Frenki's men, but all I'm clear about is SAJ, special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the reason that you're sure that the Brazil Group was an SAJ unit rather than a JSO unit is because you met them personally and they told you they were SAJ; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he told me. I believe he was the deputy or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's the only source of your information about whether they were SAJ or JSO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, yes. Later on I met more of them, I met Zika, the commander, his name was similar to mine and I knew for a fact that that was indeed the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know Zika's full name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trajkovic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And now I would like to show you the last page of these communication plans, page 3 of the B/C/S. Okay. And on this one, General, we'll see listed two subordinate units of the 125th, item number 4 and item number 7, respectively the 4th battle group -- or the 4th Combat Group and the 2nd Combat Group with call-signs Ibar 90 and Ibar 70. That's correct, isn't it, those are the code-names they used in July/August 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but again I have to say that this work-plan of the communication centre is not defined in terms of time, so I can't tell you whether it's June, July, or August. We frequently performed exercises, drills, with those stations to avoid detection of our communication and correspondence plans. They changed almost daily, but you have this one for one day and we keep going around in circles with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And number 2 we see a code-name, Pastrik 13, for the forward command post of the Pristina Corps. Is that a code-name that you associate with them in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was ten years ago. I cannot tell you whether Pastrik 13 was the commander or the Chief of Staff or the operations officer. I believe it was the commander, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm going to move away from that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, General, I would like you to help us, if you can, with a term that we've seen in many decision and orders from 1998 and 1999 by Pristina Corps and the 3rd Army regarding actions to support the MUP in dealing with terrorism, and that term is "armed non-Siptar population." You saw that term used in a number of orders that you received, didn't you, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it in those documents that went from the 3rd Army through the corps and down to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And oftentimes those orders were couched in terms that said something like this: The Pristina Corps with reinforcements and armed non-Siptar population in Kosovo and Metohija shall conduct and attack in the area of responsibility or shall support the MUP ... Who or what were the armed non-Siptar population in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will take an explanation if you want to know how I understand it. I hope you will not interrupt me if I start from the documents governing the concept of All People's Defence and social protection which defined what exactly "armed population" is. The instructions according to which we worked in those years dealt with that term "armed population," and there was a unit in the former SFRY, the JNA, now the Army of Yugoslavia [as interpreted], which had the obligation to use that term and to include it in tasks for units, that's one explanation. Another explanation, if you put armed non-Siptar or Siptar population or let it be Dutch population in the tasks for units which is paragraph 5 going on by items 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, et cetera, you have to define "armed Siptar or non-Siptar population." Unless it's defined, it's an empty phrase without meaning. I suppose that in these documents this reference meant units of civilian protection and civil defence. I hope I've succeeded in explaining it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, were there no Siptars in Kosovo in the civilian defence or the civilian protection? Were both those bodies made up entirely of non-Siptars?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were Siptars on the list in units of civilian protection and civil defence. There were some on the records for the Army of Yugoslavia, too, but they did not respond to call-ups. They did not want to receive weapons, and that's why perhaps this term was used "armed non-Siptar population" because they did not dare respond I would say to call-ups. They did not want to receive weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, is it your evidence, it is your understanding, that armed non-Siptar population in the context of these orders meant only the civil defence and civil protection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that's my understanding, and I suppose that even those people who were not in the civil protection and civil defence. Let's say that somebody is in Priluzje village far from Kosovska Mitrovica and there are only one or two persons there who have weapons, what are you going to do with them? Are you going to leave them in the lurch?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware that in 1998 some tens of thousands of Serbs in Kosovo were furnished weapons? And I'm not talking about soldiers, just civilians. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I know some were armed. I personally armed military conscripts, those who come to our brigade, 125th Brigade, in response to a call-up. And the procedure was strictly prescribed for issuing weapons, training, control, returning weapons, et cetera. As for those auxiliary organs, I believe there were around 10.000 armed persons in civilian protection and civil defence. I don't know the exact number, but I believe this is approximately the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you personally engage in arming any Serbian civilians who were not conscripts and coming into the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not have that right; if I did that, I would be criminally liable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you engage with local authorities in Kosovska Mitrovica regarding planning for the defence of populated areas in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't work together with them on that. There were local bodies that were in charge of that. There were other bodies that were in charge of that. I had a million other problems to face.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. No subordinate officer of yours was delegated to work with the municipal authorities in Kosovska Mitrovica regarding defence planning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The brigades and the combined arms tactical units lost that role. You know in which case I would have been responsible. If there was an occupation system in place, for example, but we never carried out an occupation, an act of occupation. Why would we occupy our own territory? For example, if I had crossed to Albania, to the Troje sector, that would have been an act of occupation because that was someone else's territory, just to name an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me move on and show you another exhibit, P1434. General, this is an order from the Pristina Corps command signed by General Pavkovic dated the 19th of September, 1998, to support the MUP in breaking up terrorist forces in the general Cicavica sector. We don't have delivery information on this, but could you take a look at this and tell us if you recall receiving such an order or if you remember this action?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, but could I at least see all the items, 5.1, 5.2, to see if my name is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Certainly, and I have a hard copy, it may make it easier because it's several pages.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you do recall having seen this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could go to item number 3, it's page 5 of the English; I'm not sure which page in the B/C/S. If you could would us, we could put that on the screen for the others. I see we've already got it up. I believe it's page 3 for you. Item 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It talks about the task of neighbouring units, and it talks about what MUP forces will do. The second paragraph says: "In addition part of the Serbian population in the Serbian settlements shall cut off the right bank of the Sitnica river and prevent terrorist forces from crossing ..." Do you recall whether the Serbian population was actually employed that way during this action, or was that outside the area that you were dealing with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that the Serb population was used in this way, but if that's what item 3 says, "neighbouring units," this means that this is outside the purview of the Pristina Corps. And I think this is just an empty phrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could go down to item 4 where it says: "I have decided ..." And under "objective" the second sentence says: "Engaging territorially-based MUP forces and the Serbian population, throw a wide cordon around Mount Cicavica, break up and destroy any terrorists discovered along the axis of attack and along the road." Do you recall whether the Serbian population was engaged with territorially-based MUP forces and setting up a cordon around Mount Cicavica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, let me say I do not recall that. Secondly, we were in no position to do this with the Pristina Corps and the MUP, let alone the Serb population or whoever's referred to there. This is a megalomaniac mission for someone who is believed to have no more than three armed men; therefore this is just another one of those empty phrases.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, General, I'll tell you we have evidence in this case at a VJ collegium where General Samardzic advises General Ojdanic that some 40-plus thousand Serbian civilians in Kosovo have been armed. We're not talking about just two or three people. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I assume that there were about 10.000 armed men in the district bodies, civil protection and civil defence, so that's definitely more than three of those, that it was someone else altogether who took decisions on their use, someone from the defence ministry not the army itself. And the third assignment that you see here, item 3 in relation to neighbouring units, General Pavkovic or his operatives wrote exactly what I assume the army commander's order to have stated. I suppose now we're about to see whether he handed out any specific assignments to those, specifically in item 5 or perhaps not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in item 5 let me ask you specifically about elements of the 125th. Item 5.1 has a task for the Combat Group 1 to support an attack by the 3rd Detachment of the PJP and the JSO and a PJP company from Pec. Do you know what JSO unit was involved in this action? Did you personally have any dealings with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no contact with them at the time, so this is the 3rd Detachment of the PJP Pec unit. So we were securing support for them in the second line, but behind; and the JSO, if they were there, were on the opposite side, the other end, but that's what I assume. I don't remember all these details. Perhaps I just simply wasn't that, that being the reason I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General. I'm finished with that one for now. I'd like to show you next Exhibit P3049. And so you know, this is a document from March 19th, 1999, before the NATO bombing began. And let me ask you while that's coming up, what was your understanding about the October 1998 agreement regarding the OSCE-KVM mission in terms of anti-terrorist operations or actions? Was there an obligation on the part of the Serb authorities to advise the observers before going out and engaging in those actions? What was your understanding about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the agreement that had been reached, the Pristina Corps had three units out there, and all those men that were believed to be necessary to secure the state border in depth. When there were drills, as I said yesterday, we were under an obligation to talk to the OSCE liaison officer and announce any of our drills an hour ahead of time so that they could monitor this. No restrictions were imposed on us in terms of what exactly we did in terms of drills, but there were other things that were involved. For example, if one wanted to monitor the situation along the state border, the OSCE mission itself was under an obligation to announce their arrival at least 24 hours ahead of time for them issuing activities, the paramount reason for them each to do this was their own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll give you a hard copy of this document, and you'll see this is one of those Joint Command orders that's not signed. And in item 4.4 you'll see a task listed for the 125th. Do you recall receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I received this order. This is a document produced by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And as I said, it has no signature. It has the typewritten "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija" at the end and in item number 12 it says: "The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija from the Pristina sector shall command and control all forces," right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch your last statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That says that the Joint Command was going to command and control all forces during those combat operations. That's what it says, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. This is something that was always copied each time a document like this was produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the task for the 125th was not in the border belt area, right, it's near the town of Srbica, far in the interior of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's deep inside Kosovo and Metohija, as you say, but this task strikes me as illogical now. It says the 125th Motorised Brigade, meaning in its entirety. So I'm beginning to have some misgivings. I'm no longer sure that I saw this document. I was expecting it to say something like: 125th, and then open brackets (with BG-1, BG-2) that sort of thing. I'm not sure if it was amended at any stage, I mean, this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall your unit or subordinates of your brigade participating in an action like the one described in this document in or around March 20th of 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the date on this one is the 19th of March by the so-called Joint Command, meaning the Pristina Corps, and then I transformed it into an order and task of my mine. I believe we started carrying this out at the beginning of the aggression. This was part of the preparations. This was all in order to block the road and to fend off the terrorist forces along the Kosovska Mitrovica-Pec road. I didn't travel that road. Can you imagine what that situation is like? A brigade commander who can't travel the road with his own unit, it's an embarrassment, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And at the very end it says: "Readiness for combat action, 0600 hours on the 20th of March," indeed this was an action that was carried out before the NATO bombing began, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that it began, if that's what it states, and it should have been that way but it could have been postponed. I would need to look at combat reports to know exactly. I'm not saying that's when the aggression began, I'm saying it's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That would be convenient, Mr. Hannis. We have to break here, as yesterday, Mr. Zivanovic, this break for half an hour. Could you please again leave the courtroom with the usher. [The witness stands down].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at 11.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is coming in, I'd like some guidance from the Court. By my calculations, I've reached the point used on direct examination and cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic. I have a considerable amount of material I would like to cover with this witness, and I'm asking the Court's indulgence to allow me what may be another hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you're not inclined to do that, then I'll try and adjust accordingly with what you're willing to give me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This, Mr. Hannis, I think over the piece the Prosecution has shown significant restraint in the use of time during the Defence phase of the case, and you probably have time in the bank over the piece and therefore we consider such a request to be a reasonable one in principle. So far as this particular situation is concerned, it does seem to us that you have been proceeding expeditiously throughout the cross-examination and it has been a focused cross-examination; and therefore, we are willing to grant some indulgence, but we'd like you to finish in about three-quarters of an hour or so, say five past 11.00, something of that nature. If you still feel the need to continue at that stage, please ask us again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I have a question for you concerning these action orders that were issued by the Joint Command with tasks for you. They typically list a command post from which the operation or the action is going to be commanded, and that's usually in the last item number 12 or 13. That's a standard feature of all such orders, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Normally it was the corps command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as a brigade commander, a commander of a subordinate unit, receiving these orders, is it important for you to know where that command post is or is that just extra information that doesn't really matter that much?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't matter that much to me, but it mattered to my command organs. I would order them to go to the command for correspondence and for the production of plans. I would speak to the commander. I communicated with the commander wherever he happened to be, in Pristina, in Djakovica, in Mitrovica, and so on and so forth, by radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then maybe you can help me with one issue. I'd like to show you first of all Exhibit P1966. I'll hand you a hard copy. This is dated the 22nd of March, 1999. It's another one of these unsigned Joint Command orders for routing the Siptar terrorists in the Malo Kosovo area. Do you recall having received this order? It has a task for your Combat Group 4 in item 5.2.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see in item number 13 -- well, I'm sorry. Let me go to item number 11 first under command and communications. It says: "The Pristina Corps command post shall be in the building of its peacetime location," correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's clear then that this is a document produced by the corps command and not some Joint Command that didn't exist. Can I please have item 13 because I don't have it. It must be on page 4 or page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we omitted the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's help.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, General, I'd like to hand you a related document, this is P1967, and I think you mentioned this in your direct testimony. This is also dated the 22nd of March, 1999, and you'll see it has strictly confidential number 455-56/1 and you'll see it's entitled: Amendment to the Decision. This appears to be an amendment to the one you were just looking at; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it seems to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this one is actually signed by General Lazarevic and it indicates that it was delivered to the 125th on the last page, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's right. It says in code to 125th and other units, but you see that it was signed by the corps commander on the left-hand side, which means the document was signed in order to be sent in an encrypted form. It wasn't signed on the right-hand side, which would be the usual course of action to take. I suppose this amendment was encrypted before it was sent, and I assume that's why General Lazarevic signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And my question is: This amendment appears to have only item numbers 4 and 5 in it, right? There's no item 1 through 3 and no items 6 through 13.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, because of the urgency. If there was an amendment to be made to a decision, it had to be done quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And there's no need to put in the things that are not being changed. You only need to put in the parts that are different, that are being changed, being amended, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So reading these two together, the original order and the amendment, isn't it true that the command post for this action is as stated in the original document under item number 11, the Pristina Corps command in its peacetime location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's only logical that it remained the same as in the decision that it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you would have no reason to believe that the command post for the overall action was in the village of Lausa, as is listed on the last page in the amendment, because that command post refers to the 354th in item 5.4, does it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, the 354th Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move now to -- well, do you see what your task was, task for your subordinate unit was in item 5.2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that, but may I just check for any discrepancies in relation to the original document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the discrepancy or the difference is actually quite considerable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But with regard to the task that is in the amendment, is that the task that your subordinate unit carried out, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amendment predates the previous document in as far as the items that were eventually delivered are concerned. Combat Group 4 carried out this particular task; it was not a difficult task. The previous order contained the more difficult task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you say about predates. On my copy both the amendment and the original order are dated the 22nd of March. Isn't that what it shows on your document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right, but you probably didn't understand what I was trying to say. I am saying that the older task for my unit was the one that was in the amendment. It preceded the other one, and this was the one that now took effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at exhibit 5D463, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, you'll see this is I think a combat report from your 125th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go down to the bottom of both pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Does this reflect in item 5.1.4 that: "Battle Group 4 has been engaged within the blockade," and that was the task described in those two -- in that document you were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. This combat group or some of its elements were in the Stari Trg area before. This is a radio relay hub. It was a military installation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I want to show you another one of your combat reports, 5D465. This is from the 3rd of April.
