It relates to a different action, but my question is not about the action per se. Do you recognise that? I'm sorry, I said "the 3rd of April," but I think -- I guess it's the 4th.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page of both the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in item number 5 you have a recommendation for the command where you say: "I recommend not sending volunteers to the units before they are tested by a psychologist and a security check is carried out by the security organs." Did you make that recommendation because prior to this date you'd had some problems with volunteers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had faced problems with a volunteer in two different places. In one of these places what was -- with a single volunteer and in the other place it was with three volunteers. It was in the Babaj Boks sector while secures the state border. One of them climbed an electricity post in order to repair the power lines up there, and he fell down and was killed as a consequence. Just above the village of Streoc where we were also securing the state border in depth, three volunteers clashed and killed each other. Those were the problems that I faced, and that's why I requested this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know if your recommendation was followed up on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The first round of vetting was done in the recruitment centres where volunteers were welcomed, in this case in Bubanj Potok and in Medja. The second round of vetting occurred -- they started in Pristina, which they normally didn't. The last, final round of vetting for my brigade specifically was done where my men were receiving these volunteers. I had a psychologist working for me as well as a doctor, several doctors, who were in charge of the first round.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, do you recall one of your subordinate units being involved in an action around the middle of April 1999 in the Rugova area in connection with the hydroelectric plant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the 2nd Light Infantry Battalion from the 58th Light Infantry Brigade. This was a regular military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware that the order for that particular action had passed through the attention of General Ojdanic at the Supreme Command Staff and that he had actually made some suggestions about that action? Were you aware of that or did you see any of those documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may explain, this document by the Supreme Command Staff is something that I saw as I was being proofed. I didn't know about this at the time, but I did have an order, a document, from the corps commander, the corps command to lend support to the forces at Rugovska Klisura and to the effect that a request had been sent to the 3rd [as interpreted] Army commander to use some units of the 3rd Army along the Cakor pass, Bjeluhe and Kuciste. And the date was the same as the one when the order was delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, it's line 47 and 6 and 7, he's referring to the 2nd Army, just for clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received a document to my attention from the corps commander --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's a simple translation question. Were you talking about the 3rd Army commander or the 2nd Army commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both. The commander of the Pristina Corps sent a document to the 3rd Army command in order to ask through the General Staff for the involvement of another army along this axis. Am I being sufficiently clear now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the other army was part of the 2nd Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, part of the 2nd Army. This is the Podgorica command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, the next topic I want to ask you deals with the air force, with the Yugoslav air force. How long after the start of the NATO bombing on the 24th of March did it continue to be active and have aircraft flying, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're really pressing me hard, aren't you, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think General Zivanovic is, after all, an infantry officer and that was his job at the time. He was in a brigade. He wasn't at the General Staff, he wasn't part of the air force; therefore, I don't think he can say anything about this. I don't think any answer obtained would be relevant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It hasn't prevented many army officers telling us about NATO action, Mr. Cepic. There's no reason why an army officer on the ground should not be able to tell us something about the use of the air force; after all, it's often used in combination with the army. Mr. Hannis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not trying to pin you down to a precise date and hour, but can you give me an approximate week or month? Were they still flying in mid-April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know. I asked the corps commander to have support in the Kosare area, and I never got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And when was that? Was that on --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the land and air battle took place, when it started, as of the 9th of April and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you Exhibit P2033. I can hand you a hard copy, General. And this is a regular combat report from your 125th on 28 March 1999. If you could go to the last -- last page, I think, item number 9, page 4 of the English, item number 9 says: "Do not send our aircraft when there's been notification of NATO aircraft flying over because this causes alarm among the units. We recommend that our aircraft fly over in the early hours of the morning." This was dated the 28th of March, so your planes were still flying as of the 28th, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they weren't flying. It would have been a good thing, but this was announced on an hourly basis from the operations centre of the corps command. This was something that was announced. Our planes are about to take off, our planes are about to arrive, and they never did; and then I passed the information along down to the last soldier just in case our planes eventually came to keep them from firing at our own planes. This was a huge problem that I was facing, and that is why I said this later on. So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the last part of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence of your answer, please; the interpreter did not understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So please say when they can really take off so that we might know, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, that's not what it says. It says: "Do not send our aircraft when there's been prior notification ..." That sounds to me like they have been flying. Are you saying they were not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying to you is that at least in my area there were no planes in the air, none of our planes. I'm certain about that. I received an air-raid alarm on the evening of the 23rd, and I never terminated this simply because NATO planes were flying overhead all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you next Exhibit P2038, this is four days later, another regular combat report, and I'll trade you -- hand you a hard copy of this one, and if I could have the others back.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, if you'll go to item number 4 just above your signature, it's on page 2 of the English it says: "We kindly request that commencement and termination of air-raids be signalled only by the one person on operational duty and not by several persons which causes confusion, especially if our air force is engaged." That suggests to me that your air force up until that point had been flying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely not correct. The context is entirely different. If you want me to explain, I'm glad to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I have your answer and maybe Mr. Cepic will ask you something on re-direct. I need to move along, General, and I'd like to show you next Exhibit P1246. And I'll hand you a hard copy of this one because it's several pages. This is dated the 4th of April, 1999, it's your order regarding hygiene and sanitation measures in battle-fields. You recall issuing this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my order, it was signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Vidosav Sekulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And item number 2 says: "Hygiene and sanitation measures in the battle-fields of the zone of responsibility of the 125th shall be organized and carried out by all units of the 125th, the organs of the MUP, in cooperation with the organs of authority (military prosecutors, organs of authority in the municipality and others)." And item number 7 which is on page 6 of the English, and I'm not sure which page of the B/C/S, I think it's page 7 of the B/C/S, would you have a look at that. It says: "The commanders of combat groups in the zone of responsibility ... the PKPo," can you tell me what that acronym stands for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. " ... the chiefs of the MUP in the zone of responsibility ... as well as the chiefs of the Kosovska Mitrovica and Pec districts, together with the presidents of the municipalities, shall be responsible to me," meaning you, "for the implementation of this order." So it appears that for purposes at least of battle-field sanitation and hygiene, you take the view that the MUP and the municipal authorities are answerable to you, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what this particular document reflects, but it was written by the assistant commander for logistics using the standard format contained in the instructions to comprise all of the various bodies. When I saw this several days later, I dispatched him to go and apologise to those people because I had no authority to order anything to district or municipal chiefs. But certainly sanitation work was to be performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you issue any written document withdrawing what you had said here in item 7?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was oral information received from Lieutenant-Colonel Zecevic. He issued it to everybody face-to-face, he told everyone, that is, but I was already at the border at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Next I want to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know why the standard formula for these orders did envisage the MUP and the municipal authorities being answerable to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was the idea of All People's Defence, social protection, and the place and role of everyone was envisaged in the system of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, next I'd like to show you Exhibit P1448. I'll hand you a hard copy of this one. It's also dated the 4th of April, 1999. This is from General Pavkovic at the 3rd Army command with instructions about security arrangements. Do you recall having received this order? It talks about setting up check-points.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I did not receive this document of the 3rd Army. It was the corps command that received it. Probably the corps command then issued an order to me, which I would like to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, General, I'm sorry, I don't have an order from the Pristina Corps. Do you recall receiving an order to that effect about setting up check-points?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received an order and I myself acted on that order and issued orders that two mixed check-points should be set up, and as I said yesterday one was in the area of Ibarska Slaina, a village on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other one was on the administrative border between Kosovo and Metohija and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the entire reply.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was only to check military personnel passing through -- I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's been recorded is that you received an order and you yourself acted on that order and issued orders that two mixed check-points should be set up, one in the area of Ibarska Slaina --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ibarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry -- and the other one in the municipality of Kosovo and that was only to check personnel passing through. Now, do you need to add to that answer? Has anything been omitted that's important?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second was not on the territory of Kosovo but on the territory of Savine Vode, which is on the administrative border between Kosovo and Metohija and the Republic of Montenegro, and I have nothing else to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I think we're both fast talkers and I know I'm trying to speed up, but we'll both try and slow down for the interpreter. Item number 2 in this order in the middle it says: "By engaging MUP organs, brigade commanders are to restrict civilian movement in their zones." Do you recall if the order on this topic you received from the Pristina Corps had this provision, about engaging the MUP to restrict civilian movement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this document issued by the 3rd Army command. I don't remember this being in the corps command document. It might have been, but not in a single situation did we limit the movement of civilians. Checking roads was done or monitoring roads was done by the traffic police of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And in item number 7 it talks about Pristina Corps command issuing temporary stay permits to military personnel and civilians. Do you know if that was done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably done for the members of the command. I did that for the members of my command of the 125th Brigade. Without such a pass, a soldier could not go through the check-point on Ibarska Slatina and the other one and Savina Vode; and if he did, he would have to leave his weapons behind, if he was going on leave. And on his way back, he would take the weapons back and then rejoin the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I'd like to move to Exhibit P2022. I'll hand you a hard copy with the assistance of the usher. General, this is dated the 21st of April, 1999, from your command. It's a regular combat report and it talks about in -- on page 3 of the English and the last item number 7 for you it says: "Get the Pristina MUP staff to send an order to their subordinates regarding resubordination to the units of the VJ." We see this as just a day or so after that order had come down. Do you know, was your request followed up on by the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, what order? My order or this request of mine?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, your request. Do you know if the Pristina Corps did send an -- or did do something to try to get the Pristina MUP to have their subordinates resubordinate to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there's a Pristina MUP. It's just a Pristina municipality. The commander told me that he had forwarded the request to the commander of the 3rd Army, and then further than that it was not within my purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You never saw that actually happen, did you, MUP being subordinated to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of April when I received the order on resubordination, I called the MUP chiefs or the detachment commanders and I told them what I expected from them. They said, All right, but we have to get orders or documents from our own structures, from the MUP. To the best of my knowledge, they never received those; and therefore the MUP unit was never subordinated to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. As a practical matter on the ground, in the field, in joint actions you carried out with the MUP from the beginning of the war and before there was even talk about such an order, throughout the end of the war in June was it a problem for you in carrying out these joint actions or coordinated operations, not having a piece of paper that said, MUP is subordinated to VJ? Didn't actual cooperation work successfully in the field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the war operations there was situations where this was a problem for me, and then through the chief of security in the brigade and other persons I tried to reach an agreement with the detachment commanders as regards those tasks which were of common interest. And when they agreed, I would incorporate that in my order; if they did not agree, I was unable to incorporate it in the order. Sometimes I may have told them, We will do this for your information so that you'll know where we'll be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to complain in writing or orally to General Lazarevic about problems with MUP, either not coordinating with you on actions or problems with MUP committing crimes against civilians in your area of responsibility? Did that ever happen? Did you ever complain to General Lazarevic about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did complain in conversations with him, orally. I did not really observe them committing crimes. It was more that they did not carry out certain tasks which were in my interest to be complied with. The Siptar terrorist forces from the Jablanica area were active and this got [as interpreted] in my way on the Kosare axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let me move now because I'm near my time-limit. Can you tell us what and where is the general area or sector that's been referred to as Reka? Perhaps it would help if I could show you a map, I think, P615 at page 17 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we're waiting, in 57, 1, I believe the witness said that: Went in my way in defence on the Kosare axis because he was keeping the defence line on Kosare axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, and actually I think I need to go to page 21 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It made the defence of Kosare more difficult; that's what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can go to the upper two-thirds of this page, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, does this map include the area that you referred to as Reka? You'll have to help me out because I'm not sure. And do we need to -- do we need to zoom in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here, but could you zoom in, please. Yes, we do need to zoom in, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may assist, the upper right-hand side of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We see Junik here. Can you orient me to Reka starting from Junik? Is Junik part of the -- what you call the Reka area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a little more and move it to my left? No, the other way, the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We're at the edge of this page of the map. Djakovica is on the next page of the map. Do you need to have that to help orient you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right. I can see it now. That's the part that goes from Djakovica across Pacaj, Racaj, Seremet, and Junik is not part of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Would you be able to draw it on this map for us, a rough outline of the Reka area, using the pen like you did the other day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a line here which I don't understand what it represents but -- well, it's like this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be black.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we give that an IC number, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC166, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, were some of your subordinate -- well, some of your subordinate units were participating in an action around the end of April referred to as the Reka action, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two units of mine participated in the blockade on the Smonica-Berija-Nivokaz axis. Whether the action was called Reka, well I don't know. I never received a document. It may have been referred to in that way orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at Exhibit P2024, and I'll hand you a hard copy of this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, this is a regular import from your 125th dated the 27th of April, 1999, and if you could go to item number 2 it -- well, first of all, I guess in item number 1 you'll see a reference to: "During the day at 0800 hours," do you see that, I think it's the second paragraph from the bottom in the B/C/S. "During the day at 0800 hours a column of Siptar civilians was formed on the following axis: Seremet village, Pacaj village," and further on. "We believe they want to pull out from the sector of operations of our forces in the general area of the Ramoc facility." Can you tell us what the Ramoc facility was? I see on my map what appears to be a village named Ramoc just north of Korenica. Do you know what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it's a village or a facility -- well, if it had been a village I would have used the letter "S," probably to stand for Selo, village, but I can't recall right now, it escapes me, it eludes me. I might remember later on. I think it's a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And then in item number 2 it says, second sentence: "Part of the forces is engaged in mopping up the terrain from Siptar terrorists in the general area of Reka, in keeping with your decision." What decision was that of -- and this is addressed to the Pristina Corps command and the forward command post? Was that a written decision or an oral decision or do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall. The task was issued orally by the Chief of Staff of the Pristina Corps to me. I engaged two companies in the blockade and sent an officer to Djakovica to report to one of the organs of the -- of the command post which was detached.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And refresh my memory, who was the Chief of Staff of Pristina Corps on 27 April 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As if you didn't know, he was then a colonel, Veroljub Zivkovic. Now he's a retired General.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Frankly, General, I've had some problem getting your name and his name and General Dikovic. I get all three names mixed up. Would you go to item number 6 the last sentence in that item is page 3 in the English. This is the commander's decision for the next day it says: "Part of the forces to continue mopping up the general area of Reka in a concerted action with the MUP." Do you recall that was your decision on the 27th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, but my unit or units, the two units, did not enter the Reka facility. They only held the blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I see I'm near the time-limit you gave me originally. I think I need about 10 or 15 minutes to complete everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You had actually significantly underestimated how much time you'd actually used, Mr. Hannis. So another ten minutes would simply bring you back to where you would have been if you had got it right the first time --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I want to show you P2025 which is another combat report and this is from the next day. I'll hand you a hard copy with the help of the usher. This is the 28th of April, and this is your document, correct, you see your name at the bottom? Yeah? I'm sorry, I need to have an answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Item number 2 on page 2 of the English, page 1 for you, second sentence says: "Some forces have been used to clear the terrain of Siptar terrorists in the general Reka sector, as per your decision." Which part of your forces were doing that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to those two companies which were on the Smonica-Seremete-Nivokaz axis only engaged in the blockade not in any kind of searching or mopping up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, this -- your telegram says: "Some forces have been used to clear the terrain ..." It doesn't say: Some forces have been used to maintain the blockade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. When you say "clearing the terrain," it means I'm blocking, others are searching. That's how it was done jointly according to the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And where were those two companies from again? What was their designation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One company was in the defence area of the 1st Motorised Battalion of my brigade, 125th, in the Smonica sector, and the other one was the so-called volunteer company, one platoon of those who volunteered to engage in the blockade from the howitzer division, another one from the armoured, and a third from the armoured unit. I didn't have -- or battery. I didn't have other forces, and it was very difficult up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where were you -- at the time you were writing these combat reports, where were you physically located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically I was in Rasa e Kosares and this report was written by my desk officer in the operations sector, and that's why there was sometimes problems in the wording because he didn't have a radio station, so he couldn't hear everything; and he wouldn't know everything I was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So where were he physically located writing up these combat reports?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically he was in the command post in the suburbs of Decani because the NATO forces didn't know where I was, otherwise they would have done me in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have another copy of the map at P615, page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I'm going to ask you to look at a map again, that same area we looked at before, when you drew the Reka area for me. And you'll help me out, does that map show where you were located, the border point Rasa e Kosares where you were, is that on this map? I see Kosare.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we enlarge the upper half of this page and scroll down so we have Decani at the top. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is the location where you were at on this map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. If you want me to pin-point it, please ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, could you put your initials and draw a circle around it at the approximate location where you were on the 27th, 28th, 29th of April.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And -- thank you. You've drawn a circle and then it appears to be an initial above it. Then could you draw another circle where your operations officer who was writing these reports was located. You said in the suburbs of Decani, approximately.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot draw it in precisely because I need a smaller scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could just put a number 2 and draw a circle around it in the approximate area -- okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if -- do you recall that in late April General Lazarevic came and visited your brigade, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that night. I can explain to you exactly where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you a couple questions. Did you meet with him personally during that visit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where did you meet with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I escorted him along the route that he requested. Shall I say which?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was within my disposition up to noon in the area between Rasici village and Bijelo Polje. He toured part of the tank unit, and then in this area where this mark of the command post and then above this, a kilometre to the west above Decani in the area of the positions of the artillery rocket unit of anti-aircraft defence, and in this place where I drew the command post, then he returned back to Pec. Colonel Zivkovic went back to Djakovica, and I went to my unit, up to Kosare.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you next then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could we give this an IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC167, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me show you next Exhibit P2026. If I can have the usher hand you this one. This is a combat report from your 125th dated the next day, the 29th of April, 1999. And if you could go to item 2, it's on page 2 of the English, and it's the second paragraph, the second sentence I think. It says: "Operation or action Reka was completed on 28 April," and then it mentions the 1/1 mtb and the DOB company, the volunteer company "participated in the operation from among our units," and that's what you told me about before, right? Are you finding that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I haven't. Could you point it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's on the first page of B/C/S, I think, item number 2, and it's the second paragraph, it talks about the remaining brigades are fortifying, settling up obstacles, et cetera. I may have highlighted it in orange. Do you see it says: "Operation Reka was completed on the 28th ..."?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it says it was completed successfully. If you could go down then to the next paragraph do you see where it says: "The Commander and Chief of Staff of the Pristina Corps were in the Brigade from 0900 to 1200 hours today." Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, but in the first sentence you directed me to it doesn't say "completed successfully," it says only "completed."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The last sentence in that paragraph seems to say: "The operation was completed successfully," do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see. I stand corrected. I was just looking at the first line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So was General Lazarevic then in the Decani area between 0900 and noon on the 29th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Lazarevic together with the Chief of Staff and myself, that was in the suburb of Decani, the command post that I drew on the map. He was there from 11.15 to 12.00, and then I saw him off when he left to go back to Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know approximately how far is Decani from Glogovac? Can you give me an estimate in terms of either kilometres or hours to drive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends how you go, from 90 to 112 kilometres -- sorry, 20 kilometres. If you go through Pristina, that's 120 if you go across Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If I could show you Exhibit 5D384, I have a question for you. I can give you a copy. It's just one page. This is a document dated the 29th of April from General Lazarevic alerting subordinate units to a security problem, if you will. And at the beginning he says: "At around 0900 hours on 29 April 1999, I personally came across a part of the 37th ... which was crossing a brook near Lozica village..." Now, the only Lozica village I came across is between roughly between Glogovac and Malisevo, and if that's the case how could General Lazarevic be there at around 0900 and be in Decani with your unit at 0900? You don't have any idea about that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea how a person be in two places simultaneously, but you can maybe guess that this is a typographical error and that it should have been 1900 hours, not 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand behind what I said, he was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, one more thing. There is a report in combat report you cannot --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- General, don't get me wrong. I'm not necessarily challenging you about that. Finally, I have three last questions. You told us how you taught strategy, and let me ask you a question related to strategy. We had evidence from one witness that a few days before the war he attended a meeting where General Pavkovic was talking about the NATO bombing was going to start within a few days and that one of the first things the army needed to do was - and there's some dispute about the exact wording - was to get the Albanians or to get the KLA off their back, off the army's back. Now, strictly speaking from a strategic point of view, didn't it make sense for the VJ to get all of the Albanians or as many of the Albanians as possible out of Kosovo before you were going to have to engage in the expected land invasion by NATO and NATO allies? Strictly speaking from a strategic point of view, wouldn't you agree with that? You don't want to have to fight NATO when you've got Albanians, some of whom are going to be either KLA or KLA supporters in your midst and behind you. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer you with a yes or no. You will have to allow me to explain. First of all, militarily speaking, it's correct to rout or repel or crush Siptar terrorist forces. Second, it's not true that it's desirable to throw out Siptar or Albanian civilians. The danger for us is a bit less when the population is close to us, not in as much as we would want NATO aviation to hurt them too, but the danger is less. I know that you are insinuating that there was some crime of deportation, but that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And two last questions, and this relates to some open-source material, magazine or newspaper articles that I had read or seen. One is about -- well -- I'm sorry, I'm not trying to embarrass --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have an objection in principle to newspaper articles. I wanted to question a Prosecution witness Merovci on newspaper articles, and I was not able to. Newspaper articles do not have particular significant that are not of a nature that would provide valuable information unless the authors come themselves to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cepic, you know that that's not the position that we've taken in the case. I cannot remember the circumstances relating to Merovci, but you do know the significance or otherwise of the use of a newspaper article in a question depends on the contents of the article; and therefore, depends on the particular circumstances. Mr. Hannis, the start of that question rather suggests that the reference to newspapers or magazines was quite unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's just the good-faith basis for my asking the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think you should proceed to ask the question and see if there's an objection to the question unrelated to your reliance on newspaper or magazine articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand you have a close family member who is a member of the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm glad that he's a member of the MUP and he can control me quite well, he can keep tabs on me. Yes, that's my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when did she first become a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there any -- any official cooperation between you and your wife in terms of actions in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, unfortunately. I would have liked it if we had been together at the time, but we were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I won't ask the question about whether MUP was subordinated to VJ in your household. Let me ask you the last question then. There have been -- have you been named as a person to be questioned or investigated in connection with an investigation of army members allegedly involved in assisting General Mladic? You'll have to answer out loud.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was. There are proceedings going on before the district court in Belgrade, but unfortunately I was not informed of that by my wife. I learned about it from newspapers. Although I don't know Mladic. I was corps commander, and I could only have guessed that he had moved around that peacetime zone of my corps. I hope that's the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have one answer for you and Mr. Cepic concerning the photo that was at issue before. I'm advised it was part of evidence seized from the Orahovac MUP and was presented to the OTP by a KLA member on 23 August 1999 in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to what, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation -- two questions in relation to two exhibits regarding resubordination. I will spend only two minutes or three, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right, we'll see to that. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You'll see. I'll go quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the Prosecution showed you one document with a heading "Joint Command" and then an annex to that document written by General Lazarevic, P1966 and P1967. You said both were documents of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now I just want to ask one thing. That first document, is it from some superior command, superior to the Pristina Corps? If it had been from a superior command, would General Lazarevic have been able to modify it or write an annex to it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: P1428, please now. That's a document signed by Colonel Lazarevic as Chief of Staff. P1428. Could we have it on the screen, please. That's the document which has no reference to Joint Command, neither in the heading or at the bottom. It's signed by the Chief of Staff, then colonel, Lazarevic. Is this an order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision. It is to be executed through specific tasks in the form of an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Here in point 2 it says: "Tasks for units," and all that follows are tasks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So those are orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now in point 6 it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see item 6 on page 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more page further.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It's the same order from the Chief of Staff signed by Vladimir Lazarevic, and if you will agree with me it is hereby ordered to the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija to command together with the forward command post of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Joint Command existed, then Lazarevic wouldn't have been able to issue orders to it. It means that those are his superior [as interpreted] officers, his officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let me now ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The record is wrong --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think I understood that last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can't understand it the way it's on the record. We're going to correct it now. The witness said those were his subordinate officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you confirm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said if it had been the so-called Joint Command, then he as Chief of Staff, Lazarevic, would not have been able to order this to these people. Those were his officers that he was entitled to command, his subordinate officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My last question: Do you remember that at that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I still don't understand the point, Mr. Fila, certainly in the English version. It does seem to me these are all just points of argument, but if you think there's an answer to be gained from the witness that will help please try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried twice but the translation or interpretation is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you try it a third time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were his subordinate officers that he, Chief of Staff, Colonel Lazarevic, had the right to command.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Accordingly, when this is written here it is implied that those were subordinate officers, not superior officers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You mean subordinate officers would make up the Joint Command, so is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, that the witness is saying that, not me, the witness, because Colonel Lazarevic is not able to issue orders to somebody above him. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're now suggesting the Joint Command for Kosovo comprised subordinate officers?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that something like that never existed nor did such a body exist, but what is written here has to be interpreted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All of this is matter for argument. It's not something that needed to be explored in the exceptional situation of allowing you further cross-examination of the witness. I don't think it's helpful to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not exploring. I'm asking him what that means, and the witness answers my question. What is the meaning of what is written here? Command over combat operations will be executed by the Joint Command and he's giving an explanation, some kind of explanation, and I believe you will hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's try again and hear what the explanation is. What is the explanation you're now trying to give us for this? Because you've already told us what you think Joint Command is, but it would appear that you're being invited now to deal with it specifically in the context of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if it reads "combat operations will be commanded by the Joint Command," I assert that Joint Command did not exist because if it had existed Colonel Lazarevic would not have been able to issue them orders. And since he did issue tasks - and I'm talking about this "Joint Command" - then it is a group of his own staff from the forward command post who are subordinate to Colonel Lazarevic and who are monitoring activities, conveyed all that to Colonel Lazarevic, so that he's able after that to make decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to the beginning, to the first page of this document. So you're saying that this, the Joint Command referred to in this document, is different from the Joint Command that may be meant when there's a heading "Joint Command" on the document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is purely a corps command document. In the last paragraph Joint Command is mentioned. I believe it's a matter of copying and pasting on the computer because this is a purely corps document. The Joint Command has no place in it. Am I clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, because you've already told us what you believe Joint Command to mean. Are you saying that the earlier description you gave us is of a Joint Command that's different from the Joint Command in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be different, but this was just copied. This is a purely corps command document; whether different or not, I am interpreting it as it is in this decision, in this document, and I've stated that explanation two or three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I have no further questions about this. Just one more thing. Do you know perhaps that at this time, the date of this decision, at the forward command post the Chief of General Staff, General Perisic, who was visiting and inspecting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he had come to inspect, and I recall expecting him to come to my unit in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So the Chief of General Staff was there at the forward command post you mentioned with his entourage of generals and others. In the indictment of the OTP, it says that this Joint Command included a large number of civilians in 1999 they knew only about Nikola Sainovic, they don't know about the others, they will probably find out by the end of this trial. If they had all been there and commanded units, would General Perisic have failed to observe that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He certainly would have observed that civilians were in command if they had been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer is not recorded. He said: There's no question of any civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the answer that's been given is different than that. What was your answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He certainly would have noticed, no question of any civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Fila, that last point is certainly one that was not appropriate for further cross-examination at this stage. If you had wanted to deal with matters of that nature, they should have been dealt with at the appropriate stage when you could have cross-examined the witness. This is not a matter that you were only alerted to by the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: which you seek the privilege of further cross-examination to avoid an unfair trial in situation where you're making that request after the completion of the Prosecution cross-examination. Now, Mr. Aleksic, do you have a similar motion to make? Please sit down, Mr. Fila. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am not requesting your leave to cross-examine the witness. Bearing in mind that the name of my client was mentioned several times yesterday and today, I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber only to some exhibits which are already in evidence. I don't want to present arguments, I don't want to ask questions of this general, just give the numbers of the exhibits to the Trial Chamber. I need two minutes for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If these exhibits are already part of the case, then you can deal with them in your submissions in due course. There's no need for this to take up time in court. And if you feel the particular need to notify us, then you can make a written filing to that effect. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have many questions. But before we go to break, with your leave, just one correction in transcript page 75, line 6 or line 10 the answer is: He certainly would have; but I think the witness, I'm certainly. Just one correction and after the break I would like to examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The matter's dealt with in line 10 when he was given a second opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying that that's wrong or are you accepting that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he clarified. He clarified later. Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In that relation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have to break again, Mr. Zivanovic, this time for an hour. Could you again go with the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at 1.45. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It will just be a moment, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for that may I just announce that I've been assisted by an intern, Shaban Biesley [phoen] the last day and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Cepic, your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm blaming my watch. I never blame myself, Your Honour. My watch, and it truly is, and Mr. Ivetic can verify that. You know, I've never been late for court in my entire life, this is the first time, and I sincerely apologise to the court and to my client, General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sepenuk. There will be a whip around for a new watch for Mr. Sepenuk. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, it's me again, and we'll have enough time. Let us start from the very end. My learned friend Mr. Hannis mentioned the proceedings in Belgrade. You explained that you had occupied the position of the commander of the Belgrade corps. Since General Mladic was mentioned, was there a General Zivanovic in the Army of Republika Srpska subordinated to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose it was a case of mistaken identity. There is a Zivanovic, I believe, Milorad.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: At any rate, it's not you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remembered, it's Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Hannis asked you about check-points and you answered that you had set up check-points manned by the MUP and the army. Did you set up complete check-points for both the MUP and the army or only for the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were joint check-points of the MUP and the army at the exit from Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And who was answerable for what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the soldiers and policemen at a check-point were responsible only for checking the passage of military personnel and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And who sets up check-points, one body or both bodies separately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same location as far as these two check-points are concerned. The MUP patrol controls the other part according to its own regulations, and we control only the army part, the army component, military vehicles, soldiers on foot, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So I'm proceeding from the end. Towards the very end my learned friend Mr. Hannis asked a number of questions in relation to your activities on the 27th, 28th, and 29th April. He asked you, and that's on page 63 of today's transcript: Where were you in those three days, to which you drew a position on the map at the location Rasa e Kosares. I am interested in the 29th. You mentioned that General Lazarevic had arrived from Pristina on his way to Pec or on the road to Pec. Tell me, when did General Zivkovic come?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came from Djakovica to Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To clarify one point regarding a place, I have a map. Unfortunately we cannot use the Kosovo atlas for this without a complete map, so I would like this map placed on the ELMO to clarify one thing that Mr. Hannis concentrated on in his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Just for clarification, at page 79, line 12, you asked the question: "Tell me, when did General Zivkovic come?" And the answer is: "He came from Djakovica to Pec." Was that what you had wanted, the direction that he came from is what --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My question was: From where, from where--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- Where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you need additional clarification, I can ask additional question if it is necessary for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: I think it should now be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we found a map. This road that you marked, Pec-Pristina, on which you said General Lazarevic travelled, look carefully and try to find a place called Lozica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we stretch the map so as to see Pristina and Pec, open it wide. Still a bit more. Can we zoom in a bit more -- [In English] zoom out. [Interpretation] I would like to see the end points, Pec and Pristina, and after that we would zoom in to see it more clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Zoom out further so that we can see the whole of the map, we can see the edge at both sides. Will it not go any further? No. We're at our technical limit, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave, could we fix the map on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How do you mean fix it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's okay. Just a little bit on the right side and we will see the Pec also. We see the Pristina in the upper -- right upper corner. Opposite side, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Move it to the right so Pristina is right on the edge of the screen. Further, you can go another couple of centimetres, a bit more. That's it. Thank you. Still not enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We saw the main route.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can move the map a but further to the right, there is Pec. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, could you follow the main road and try to find a place called Lozica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we saw that Pristina is there, this is a road that goes from Pristina to Pec, and here is Lozica here by the road from Pec via Dolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you put a little circle around it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Pristina, Kosovo Polje, there's the road that goes to Pec and crosses here and reaches Pec. This place here is Lozica, right here. If the scale is 1:200.000, then it's 35 kilometres or 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we zoom in, please, Lozica village area of Lozica, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a brook that we can see around Lozica? Just around Lozica is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's this brook here that we can see, and it flows into Lozica village.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. At an optimum speed driving, how much time is it from this place to Pec?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this place to Pec, when the road is nearly empty, it's 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need this on the ELMO any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how long did you say it took to go from Pec to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I asked him for the distance between the village of Lozica to Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I'm asking a different question. How long would it take to go from Pec to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in view of the car General Lazarevic had at the time, he would have needed 40, 45 minutes, and that is 70 kilometres or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have on our screens IC166, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, this line of blockade by your forces, where was it, if you could show me, and the disposition of terrorist forces in the environs, I mean the 27th and 28th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this red? The line of blockade here is Smonica -- no, no, I don't need the blue to denote us. UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: [Interpretation] It's good for your wife.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Smonica, here is Berija, Nivokaz, that's the line of blockade by the two platoons I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: By two companies, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In that area, could you please draw in to the best of your recollection the terrorist forces in blue?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. It's along this entire road. That's where the Siptar terrorist forces were located. I believe they were even in this place called Seremet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, strategically speaking, and yesterday I asked you about it as did Mr. Hannis today we're talking about river valleys, you said that from Kosare your line of defence -- if your line of defence had been broken in how much time would the terrorist units link up with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Kosare-Junik-Djakovica line they would -- it would take them two hours if they were going on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you draw that line, too, in blue from Kosare to Reka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Since you used to teach strategy, would you say that this configuration of terrain allows for a rapid advance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it does because it goes downhill all the way from Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now, the movement of the population was described in your report, P20 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I must say, I don't understand this now. I thought you were talking about the breaking of the line of defence. The line of defence is between the terrorist forces and the border, and this blue line that's been drawn is behind the area, the Reka area, where the forces were. Could you explore that more. I don't understand what that blue line means.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, strategically, militarily speaking, would you explain why you drew the line this way, not through the villages marked below. Was that a possible line of attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, by one axis it's impossible for several thousands of attackers to go. They would go Tropoje, Morina, and they would encompass all this area and they would link up -- the wedge would be in Djakovica and outside Djakovica so that the entire area of Reka would be encompassed. So this is the front line of attack, and I will now draw, if you wish, where my positions were on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you do that, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It must be my fault. I thought you were blockading the terrorists in the Reka area from getting to the border. Is it the reverse, you're blocking the border to prevent people from there joining up with the terrorists in Reka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was not blocking the border; I was performing defence by relying on the very state border, defence of my country, whereas terrorists were in the area of Reka. And the objective of this attack from the Republic of Albania, Siptar terrorist forces, parts of the Army of the Republic of Albania with the support of NATO was to link up with the Siptar terrorist forces that were behind my lines in my defence area. I hope I was clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. It's the opposite from what I thought that you were describing earlier. It must be my mistake. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did these Siptar terrorist forces in the Reka area, were they located behind your back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because if you look in this part here, that's where my forces were and that's the forward edge from here, Morina border post.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mark it with a 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 is Morina border post. This part here is the 1st Motorised Battalion. This is one of its companies, 2nd Company, 3rd Company here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area of defence of one battalion. You see where the terrorist forces are, behind the area of defence of the battalion, and they are jeopardizing this segment here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To provide a full picture as long as we are on the drawing board --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the drawing board would leave anyone reading this transcript now totally lost. I don't know how anyone who takes up the transcript is going to be able to understand where any of the lines have been drawn. We've now got three more lines at the border. We were working with just one line of blockade where the 3 is. I don't know what the dotted line, blue line, along the bottom is. I understand the point that the witness is making in general, but putting individual units in particular locations and showing movement is not something I'm at all clear about now. Unless the very particular location is vital to your point, it would have been far better to have the witness just describe what was happening and describe it more fully than has happened so far. I think we should scrap this plan and start again, Mr. Cepic, but it's a matter for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like a clean map in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, on this map I would just like you to draw the attack. General, please draw in the Reka valley terrorist positions, lines of attack from the Republic of Albania against the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and the forces of defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we need to know more than that the terrorists were in the red area that we've got there along the line of the road? Do we need any more than that? If we do, please do it; but if we don't, let's not complicate the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think the General was quite clear in the examination-in-chief speaking of these matters and this clarifies, at least for me, the situation in that territory in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, just for the record, explain succinctly what happened there on the 27th and the 28th, the attack from Albania and the possibility that the integrity and sovereignty of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia would be put in danger. Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Constant attacks, a frontal attack from the Republic of Albania on the Kosare-Junik axis placed my brigade in a delicate position. There were respective Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Reka, which is from Djakovica through the valley down to Junik, as I marked here. There was a danger that my forward end would succumb that the aggressor might break through my defence line in the broader area of Rasa e Kosares and join up with the Siptar terrorist forces in the valley of Reka drawn here. If that happened, I would have failed to perform the task [Realtime transcript read in error "telephone conversation] I had received from General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Just one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Cepic, again. One of the things you said, Mr. Zivanovic, was that the terrain allows for a rapid advance because it goes downhill all the way from Djakovica. Now, Djakovica downhill in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry if I made a slip of the tongue. I said from the Kosare border post it goes downhill towards Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, that makes sense now. You see, you understand why we're finding this difficult that we have to take it -- if it's to be as detailed as this it has to be taken slowly and clearly. All right, Mr. Cepic, please continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, just for the same sake of clarity, 87, 6 and 7, in the -- the witness I believe said 87, 6, that join up with the terrorist forces in the valley, and he wasn't mentioning any telephone conversation with General Lazarevic but the order from General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Zecevic. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, just those two units from your forces that you mentioned in response to a question from Mr. Hannis. What was their function in that area where they engaged in active combat? Did they move or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit that was in the area of Smonica, Stupce as it's -- sorry, Stuble was a company from the 1st Motorised Battalion that was engaged in defence, its front facing the Tropoje marking on this map. As for the volunteer company, that is what I explained a minute ago, that was put together by using manpower from three other units was above Junik and towards Djocaj village. I additionally dispatched that unit and told them to leave this line, Stuble, and continue on to the blockade at Nivokaz.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were they performing any active operations or were they ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their task was to block the area along this line. If there were any terrorists on the move and trying to cross the line, they were to engage them, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now let's move on to something else. Mr. Ivetic asked you about that map this is 676 in e-court, could that map please be displayed on our screens. [In English] 6D676, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, sir, you've seen this map before. Can we just go through it briefly. Why do we see the MUP forces marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I got them in that document by the corps command. It said that Combat Group 3 should lend support to the MUP forces, the 8th Detachment, and the Djakovica Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you draw any maps for the benefit of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the established practice. We all did our own maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. P2113, please. This is your order, sir. Mr. Hannis was showing you this order yesterday. Please go straight to item 2 of this, paragraph 2, it says: "Prepare and plan every operation of the unit beforehand ..." And before that it states --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Cepic please speak up and speak more clearly for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you'll need to speak up if you're going to be talking away from the microphone --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- so the interpreters can hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, and I apologise especially to interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, can you please look at item 2 of this order dated the 7th of July, 1998. Does this not confirm your words to the effect that each command within its own chain ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each command does its own work, does all of its maps and decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. Yesterday you were asked by my learned friend Mr. Hannis something about 1998, and you said that at the forward command post of the Pristina Corps in Djakovica in 1998 there was Colonel Lazarevic. What precisely was his duty at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to an order by the corps commander, he was in charge of the control over the forward command post team at Djakovica. In terms of his function, he was the Chief of Staff and the deputy Pristina Corps commander too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My learned friend Mr. Fila and yesterday my learned friend Mr. Hannis showed you OTP Exhibit P12 -- 1428. This is an order on the Slup and Voksa action dated the 14th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
